jobs.title: Transitions of Care RN Case Manager
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Transitions of Care RN Case Manager based in United States.

This remote role supports high-risk patients during the critical 30 days following hospital discharge.

You will provide short-term, telephonic, interdisciplinary care management focused on preventing avoidable readmissions.

The role combines clinical assessment, patient education, care coordination, and advocacy.

You will build individualized care plans that address medical, psychosocial, medication, and resource-related needs.

Working closely with nurses, physicians, social workers, primary care providers, and community resources, you will help patients navigate complex care journeys.

The environment is collaborative, technology-enabled, and focused on measurable outcomes and exceptional patient experiences.

This is an opportunity to make a direct difference for vulnerable patients while helping shape innovative approaches to healthcare delivery.

Accountabilities

Engage recently discharged, high-risk patients by phone to understand their needs, priorities, barriers, and available support, using technology and data tools to guide care.
Conduct comprehensive assessments covering comorbidities, prior emergency department visits and hospitalizations, medications, psychosocial factors, and patient preferences.
Develop individualized care plans with patients and caregivers, defining problems, goals, and interventions while monitoring progress and adjusting plans as needed.
Educate patients and caregivers about chronic conditions, warning signs, medication adherence, exacerbation planning, and other strategies that support safer recovery.
Identify clinical and social risk factors, respond to warning signs, and proactively close gaps in care.
Coordinate closely with nurse practitioners and physicians to facilitate smooth handoffs, appropriate follow-up, and continuity throughout the post-discharge period.
Connect patients with appropriate clinical services, community-based organizations, social support, durable medical equipment, and other resources.
Collaborate with primary care partners and interdisciplinary teams to deliver evidence-based, accessible, and effective care.
Serve as a patient advocate, helping individuals and caregivers understand complex medical information and confidently navigate the healthcare system.

Requirements

Hold an unrestricted U.S. Compact Registered Nurse (RN) license and be able to obtain additional state licenses as required.
Bring 3–4 years of RN care management or telephonic case management experience.
Be available Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. MST/PST, with preference for candidates located in CT, MT, or PT time zones.
Demonstrate strong clinical assessment, analytical thinking, problem-solving, and care-planning abilities.
Communicate complex medical information clearly and compassionately using plain language.
Be comfortable spending significant time on the phone building trust with patients and caregivers, educating them, and coordinating their care.
Work effectively in an environment guided by productivity, performance, quality, and patient-experience metrics.
Demonstrate adaptability, empathy, sound judgment, organization, and a strong commitment to patient advocacy.
Health insurance experience, particularly Medicare Advantage, is preferred.
Experience with Special Needs Plans, population health, transitions of care, or related case/care management is a plus.

Benefits

Annual salary range of $85,000–$100,000, with actual compensation based on qualifications, experience, education, certifications, licensure, skills, and work location.
Employer-sponsored medical, dental, and vision coverage with low or no employee premiums.
Generous paid time off.
$100 monthly mobile or internet stipend.
Stock options for all employees.
Bonus eligibility for eligible roles.
Parental leave program.
401(k) retirement savings program.
Additional benefits included in the comprehensive total rewards package.
Fully remote work environment.

jobs.title: Substance Use Disorder Professional/Case Manager
jobs.description:
Description

The Substance Use Disorder Professional/Case Manager (SUDP) will provide culturally relevant Substance Use Disorder (SUD) services to Tribal members and other clients. This position includes conducting assessments, creating treatment plans, offering counseling, and ensuring continuity of care through case management and follow-up.

Essential Duties

Provide substance use disorder services to Tribal members and other clients, including intakes, assessments, referrals, individual treatment plans, UAs, group and individual counselling and education and documentation of client care provided.
Serve as the lead with Tribal member requests for case management. Including but not limited to:
Requests for inpatient and/or referred care including emergency and/or crisis situations according to the policy and process in place to ensure the requests are processed quickly and the appropriate level of care is coordinated with external agencies and/or facilities.
Monitor care received from external agencies and/or facilities to ensure inpatient and/or residential care received is the appropriate level of care. If the Tribal member is returning to ambulatory care provided by Snoqualmie Behavioral Health Services (SBHS) or another agency, provide the client with transition planning.
Plan and implement follow-up or aftercare programs for Tribal members discharged from external agencies or facilities providing inpatient or residential care services, so continuity of care is in place.
Provide Tribal members with information about addiction issues and services/programs available, making appropriate referrals when necessary.
Attend relevant training sessions including evidence-based and promising practices for SUD and the provision of culturally relevant care to increase knowledge and skills.
Prepare for and participate in SBHS care management meetings and/or SBHS staff meetings that support Tribal member or client’s access to care and transition planning or support services.
Consistently document all care, education and case management provided in the electronic health record.
Update annual paperwork for clients receiving services.

Additional Duties

Attend clinical supervision meetings with SUDP’s and staff cases and/or conduct educational meetings including review of individual service plans, diagnosing and meeting medical necessity within client files; attend other meetings as designated by the clinical supervisor.
Maintain continuing education requirements per WAC 246-811 and develop a SUDP Enhancement Plan with the SUD Clinical Supervisor.
The Tribe values its commitment to community service and the well-being of its members. In recognition of this, each employee may be expected to perform duties from time to time which may not be related to their regular responsibilities.
Other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Knowledgeable and aware of historical trauma and how it impacts Native American individuals today; must be culturally competent and sensitive towards the needs of this population.
Proficiency in Diagnostic and Statistical Manual, version 5 (DSM-5) American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) criteria as it relates to diagnosis.
Proficiency in the use of ASAM Placement Criteria and the 4 Quadrants of Care.
Excellent communication skills and ability to prioritize and work independently, including receiving and otherwise obtaining client information from all relevant sources, strong organizational skills
Proficiency with receiving, maintaining, documenting, or transmitting confidential Tribal member and/or client records or other confidential information according to 42CFR part 2, HIPAA, and relevant Washington Administrative Codes (WACs).
Ability to help maintain an environment that encourages teamwork, interdependence, and ethical behavior.
Ability to take directions and follow through with recommendations of supervisor.
Previous experience working in Tribal communities preferred.
Strict adherence to the code of ethics that governs the substance use disorders profession.
Evenings and weekends may be required

Education & Experience

Education Required:

Associate’s degree in Substance Use Disorder Studies by a Washington State Department of Health approved college

Experience

Previous experience with Tribal communities preferred.
Previous experience with Resource Patient Management System, Electronic Health Records preferred.
Updating and using relevant knowledge such as Microsoft Office Suite, Adobe Acrobat, PowerPoint, or other relevant software to achieve the duties and responsibilities for the position.

Certifications/Licenses

Current certification as a Substance Use Disorder Professional in Washington State.
CPR and 1st Aid certified.
Valid Washington State Driver’s License without restrictions.

Other Requirements

Must be able to pass a thorough pre-employment background investigation.
Must agree to be subject to the Tribe's Controlled Substance and Alcohol Testing Policy to include pre-employment screening.
If a former participant in SUD treatment, must have completed treatment and maintained recovery for a minimum of five years before employment.

Work Environment

The work environment includes an office environment in a controlled atmosphere building. Some remote or hybrid work arrangements may be possible in accordance with the Tribe’s Telecommuting Policy.

Tribal Preference

The Snoqualmie Indian Tribe follows the Tribal Hiring Preference as outlined in tribal policies, including the Tribal Employment Rights Ordinance (TERO). TERO sets forth certain hiring preferences for qualified individuals who are enrolled in a federally recognized Indian tribe, as well as, in some cases, preference for certain family members of those individuals.

Additional Information

Salary, compensation will be determined based on experience and starts at $76,159.67 per year.
This position is a regular full-time position and employment is at will.

Location:

Snoqualmie, WA

Benefits

First of the month following date of hire - competitive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance benefits for all regular full-time employees.
After 90 days - 401k retirement plan with employer matching contributions up to 4%.
Paid Holidays - Up to 18 paid holidays are offered every calendar year, which includes the workdays between Christmas Eve and New Year’s Day.
Paid Time Off – Employees accrue 12+ days sick and vacation leave respectively. Increases based on years of service.

Additional Perks

Additional time off opportunities available including bereavement, military, parental and jury duty.
Childcare subsidy for children enrolled full-time in the Snoqualmie Tribe Child Development Center.
Employee discounts at Snoqualmie Casino (tickets/events, gift shop and restaurants), Salish Lodge & Spa (rooms, spa & dining) and Crescent Market (gas discount card).
Third party perks include movie tickets, theme parks, shows and attractions & more.
Employee assistance plans.

jobs.title: Education Specialist
jobs.description:
Weekly outpatient therapy isn't always enough, and a trip to the ER isn't the only answer. Patients and their families rely on Compass Health Center when in crisis – every day, we help people overcome depression, anxiety, suicidality, obsessions/compulsions, trauma, chronic pain, and other obstacles in order for our patients to live freely.
About This Role

As an Education Specialist, you’ll work thoughtfully with our adolescent patients to transition students from their schools to Compass, help them execute on their school IEPs and supervised learning plans, and help re-integrate patients back into their day-to-day lives after program. This role will consist of partnering closely with the entirety of our treatment teams, including Group Therapists, Family Therapists, and Prescribers to ensure comprehensive and compassionate care. We are seeking an experienced Education Specialist who is passionate about working with children and adolescents who have a range of diagnosis in mood and anxiety disorders.  

Note: this position will start at the beginning of next school year, August 2026.

What You'll Do

Work closely with team members to support the educational needs of PHP patients
Send medical certification and release of information to home school
Communicate with patients’ home schools
Coordinate assignments with the patients’ home schools
Provide parents/guardians with educational updates
Complete educational assessment with patients to determine needs
Create academic plans with patients
Partner with clinical staff to develop and administer Executive Functioning group sessions
Assist patients with executive functioning skills
Proctor school assessments as needed
Chart communication with parents, schools, and patients
Attend rounds daily
Participate in family sessions when appropriate to provide information about school progress
Provide insurance utilization team with educational updates
Meet with patients to prepare for return to school meetings
Coordinate and facilitate return to school meetings and any other school meetings
Prepare proper documentation for school when patient returns
Update the team about transition plan and school staffing
Meet with IOP team to communicate transition goals
Other duties as assigned

Who You Are:

Masters level degree in the field of education 
Active LBS1 teaching license (required)
Experience working in a public school setting with students who have emotional disabilities 
Knowledge of school systems, special education processes, IEPs, etc. 
Experience with classroom management 
Experience with students and families in crisis 
Excellent time management skills 

We are committed to a fair and equitable work environment. The expected compensation range for this role is below. This range includes multiple career path levels across the organization; where you fall in the range is dependent upon a number of factors including, but not limited to, your years of experience, type of experience, location, and education/certifications. Compass reserves the right to update these ranges.
Compensation: $65,000 USD - $75,000 USD
We know job descriptions can be intimidating, so if this sounds like an opportunity for you, please don't hesitate to apply!  
Who We Are

Compass Health Center is a recognized leader in crisis-level mental health, bringing passion, connection, and patient-centered care to the Partial Hospitalization and Intensive Outpatient space (PHP/IOP). Based in Chicagoland, we serve hundreds of patients every day, ranging from ages 5 through adulthood, in our onsite facilities or through our flourishing virtual programming. Compass fills a critical gap between outpatient and inpatient care through an intermediate level of Behavioral Healthcare.    
A few more things we want you to know: our values are super important to us, and hopefully will be to you, too. Cultural humility, teamwork, continuous improvement, connection, patient centered care, passion, innovation, and agility should be your power sources. Joining Compass is an opportunity to feel fulfilled through a joint mission towards healing our communities. 
Benefits & Perks

We know that you will be dedicated to your purpose here. We look at that investment as a two-way street. We are proud to offer plenty of space for growth, and opportunities to pursue continuous development within our organization.

About Community HealthWorks

Community HealthWorks (CoHeWo) advances health equity by helping individuals and families access the health coverage, care, housing support, and community services they need to thrive. We work at the intersection of healthcare and community support, partnering with managed care plans, health systems, community-based organizations, and government agencies to remove barriers to care.

Community Health Workers are central to this work. They serve as trusted connectors who help people understand complex systems, identify their own goals, and take practical next steps toward greater health and stability.

Position Summary

The Community Health Worker, CalAIM works primarily in the community with Medi-Cal members who may be experiencing homelessness, multiple chronic health conditions, behavioral health needs, substance use, or other barriers to care.

Through California’s CalAIM initiative, the CHW provides Enhanced Care Management, coordinated support for complex health and social needs, and Community Supports, including housing-focused services that help eligible members work toward stability. The CHW carries an active caseload and works closely with health plans, providers, housing and benefits systems, community partners, and other CoHeWo teams. This is a non-clinical, non-supervisory role.

What This Work Looks Like

This is a relationship-based, field-focused position. Approximately 60% of the work takes place in the community and 40% involves documentation, phone outreach, service coordination, team meetings, and follow-up. Work may occur in shelters, encampments, homes, clinics, hospitals, government offices, housing locations, and partner sites.

Plans may change during the day based on a member’s circumstances. The work requires flexibility, clear communication, sound judgment, and the ability to work independently while remaining connected and accountable to the team.

A Day in the Life

You may begin your day by reviewing your caseload, responding to messages, and coordinating with teammates or a health plan. You might then meet a member at a shelter, encampment, clinic, government office, or prospective housing location to complete an assessment, prepare for an appointment, replace an identification document, apply for benefits, or work through a setback in a care or housing plan.

Later, you may accompany a member to an important appointment, coordinate with a provider or partner, connect someone with an essential resource, and document the services provided. No two days will look exactly the same, but timely follow-through and accurate documentation are always part of the work.

What You’ll Do

Member engagement and direct support

Conduct in-person and telephone outreach to Medi-Cal members identified for Enhanced Care Management or Community Supports.
Build respectful, trusting relationships and help members identify their goals, understand their options, and take practical next steps.
Meet members in community settings and accompany them to medical, housing, benefits, and other important appointments when appropriate.
Connect members with essential resources such as food, clothing, water, shelter, transportation, and community-based services.
Provide support during urgent or emotionally difficult situations, follow organizational safety and escalation practices, and recognize the limits of CoHeWo’s non-emergency role.

Healthcare, Benefits, And Housing Coordination

Complete required health, housing, and social-needs assessments and develop service plans with members.
Help members obtain or maintain health coverage, establish primary care, follow up on healthcare needs, and communicate with health plans and providers.
Support housing navigation, including housing-readiness documents, referrals, applications, prospective housing opportunities, and move-in coordination.
Help members obtain identification, Social Security cards, income verification, and other documents needed to access services or housing.
Connect eligible members with behavioral health, substance-use, County Mental Health, System of Care, and other appropriate services.
Coordinate with CoHeWo teams and external partners to reduce gaps and duplication in services.

Documentation, communication, and teamwork

Maintain timely, complete, and accurate member records, service notes, assessments, activity logs, mileage logs, referrals, and required reports.
Use assigned electronic systems and standard office technology to track services, follow-up needs, and outcomes.
Protect member privacy and comply with HIPAA, confidentiality requirements, and organizational policies.
Participate in supervision, team meetings, case conferences, training, and community meetings.
Communicate changes, safety concerns, barriers, and situations requiring guidance to the appropriate supervisor or team member.

What Success Looks Like

Successful CHWs do not solve every problem for a member. They consistently help people understand their options, move toward self-identified goals, and remain connected to available support. Success in this role includes:

Building trust while respecting each member’s autonomy, privacy, and choices.
Following through on commitments and communicating when circumstances change.
Completing accurate documentation and required follow-up within established timelines.
Using sound judgment, professional boundaries, and organizational safety practices.
Working collaboratively and knowing when to ask for consultation or support.
Responding to setbacks with patience, curiosity, and a focus on practical next steps.

What Can Be Challenging About This Work

The people we serve may be navigating homelessness, serious health conditions, behavioral health needs, substance use, involvement with the justice system, or the effects of trauma. You may support someone through an urgent situation, witness difficult living conditions, experience setbacks after significant effort, or encounter circumstances that cannot be resolved immediately. Progress is rarely linear, and members may make choices that differ from what you would choose for them.

This work requires patience, emotional presence, adaptability, and professional boundaries. It also requires recognizing your own response to difficult circumstances, using supervision appropriately, and remaining effective without taking sole responsibility for another person’s outcome.

How CoHeWo Supports You

Employees are expected to ask for support and are not expected to navigate complex situations alone. Support for this role includes:

Structured onboarding, field shadowing, and reverse shadowing before independent work.
Regular supervision, case consultation, and team-based problem solving.
Training in core practices, professional boundaries, field safety, and required program systems.
Clear escalation pathways and guidance about the limits of the role.
Access to employee wellbeing and mental health resources available through CoHeWo’s benefits programs.

Requirements:

What We’re Looking For

Required

High school diploma or GED.
Ability to build respectful relationships with people from varied backgrounds and life circumstances.
Clear communication, organization, confidentiality, and consistent follow-through.
Comfort learning and using electronic documentation systems, email, and Microsoft Office tools.
Ability to work independently in community settings while remaining accountable and connected to a team.

Relevant Experience That May Help You Succeed

Relevant experience may come from paid work, volunteering, education, caregiving, community involvement, or lived experience that you choose to share. Applicants do not need to meet every preferred qualification to be considered. Helpful experience may include:

Community health, outreach, peer support, case management, health navigation, housing services, behavioral health, substance-use services, or work alongside people experiencing homelessness.
Knowledge of Medi-Cal, CalAIM, Sacramento’s housing and benefits systems, or local health and social-service resources.
Community Health Worker, peer-support, substance-use, behavioral-health, or health-coverage enrollment training or certification.
Postsecondary education in social work, behavioral health, public health, or a related field.

Requirements

Valid California Class C driver’s license, current auto insurance, reliable transportation, and ability to travel throughout Sacramento County and surrounding areas.
Completion of a criminal background check. Findings will be reviewed in relation to the position and in accordance with organizational policy and applicable law.
Compliance with health-screening, certification, safety, and partner-site requirements applicable to the assignment.
Maintenance of required training, certifications, and renewals associated with the role.

Work Environment & Schedule

This is a full-time, non-exempt position, typically Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required based on member or program needs. Work schedules are subject to change. Approved overtime will be compensated in accordance with applicable law and organizational policy.

Community-based work may involve variable weather, uneven terrain, noise, interruptions, animals, limited sanitation, or other environmental conditions. Employees are expected to assess conditions, follow field-safety practices, and consult a supervisor when circumstances exceed the role’s scope or can no longer be approached safely.

Physical & Emotional Demands

The employee must be able to frequently sit, stand, walk, speak, listen, use a computer, write, and operate standard office equipment. Fieldwork may include walking on uneven terrain. The employee may occasionally bend, stoop, kneel, reach, climb or balance, and lift or move approximately 10–15 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

The role includes regular interaction with people experiencing emotionally sensitive, urgent, or unpredictable circumstances. The employee must be able to communicate effectively, use sound judgment, maintain appropriate professional boundaries, follow safety and escalation procedures, and seek supervision or support when needed.

How To Apply

To apply, please submit:

A resume describing your relevant experience and skills.
A brief cover letter explaining your interest in Community HealthWorks, what draws you to this position, and how your experience, skills, or perspective would help you contribute in the role.

We appreciate your interest in joining Community HealthWorks.

The ideal candidate is focused on providing culturally responsive services to unhoused women, living on Skid Row, who have experienced long-term homelessness and have been historically underserved by traditional housing programs. This innovative program is dedicated to implementing the recommendations of the Ad-Hoc Committee on Black People Experiencing Homelessness and the Ad- Hoc Committee on Women Experiencing Homelessness and is designed to quickly and permanently house the most vulnerable women of Skid Row. Provide culturally responsive field-based case management services to the most vulnerable women living in the Skid Row area to secure housing, including landlord engagement, identification of housing locations in the community, conducting biopsychosocial assessments, creating individual service plans, including goals to ensure housing stability, and ensuring women are linked to the appropriate services

Collaborate with community service providers to identify appropriate clients through educational presentations and street outreach, as needed

jobs.description:
Description

FLSA Status:
Full-time, Non-Exempt

Compensation:
$28.00-$38.69 per hour

Post Date:
August 26, 2026

September 09, 2026

Report to: Project Manager

To apply for this position:
Please submit a resume and cover letter. Your resume will not be considered if a cover letter is not included.

About Community HealthWorks

Community HealthWorks (CoHeWo) advances health equity by helping individuals and families access the health coverage, care, housing support, and community services they need to thrive. Community Health Workers are central to this work, serving as trusted connectors who help people understand complex systems and take practical next steps toward greater health and stability.

Position Summary

The Community Health Worker (CHW), Lead is an experienced CHW who continues to provide the full range of direct CHW services while also serving as a day-to-day practice resource for other CHWs. The Lead builds trusted relationships with clients, completes assessments, develops person-centered goals and service plans, coordinates care and housing-related supports, connects clients with resources, documents services, and follows through on identified needs.

In addition to maintaining an assigned caseload, the Lead supports onboarding, shadowing, coaching, consistent workflows, documentation quality, team coverage, and practical problem-solving. Because time is allocated to these Lead responsibilities, the Lead will generally carry a smaller caseload than other CHWs in the same assignment. Caseload size and complexity may vary based on client needs, staffing, program requirements, and team priorities.

This is a leadership role without formal supervisory authority. The Lead does not approve time off, issue corrective action, complete performance evaluations, or replace the Project Manager. Instead, the Lead observes work, models effective practice, offers clear and respectful feedback, identifies questions or learning needs, and communicates relevant themes to the manager.

This opportunity is currently assigned to CalAIM-funded services. CoHeWo uses a shared CHW Lead model across service areas, so assignments and specific responsibilities may evolve based on organizational, community, partnership, and funding needs. The common purpose is to provide person-centered CHW services while helping the team apply CoHeWo’s practices consistently.

What This Work Looks Like

This is a direct-service CHW position with additional Lead responsibilities. The Lead maintains relationships with assigned clients and is accountable for timely outreach, assessment, care planning, navigation, referrals, coordination, documentation, and follow-up. The current assignment includes integrated care and housing-related support for people who may have complex medical, behavioral health, housing, and social needs.

Alongside their own client work, a Lead may shadow a new employee, demonstrate how to complete an assessment or service note, coach someone through a difficult client interaction, review documentation for learning opportunities, provide team coverage, facilitate a short training, or participate in a partner meeting—all within the same week.

The Lead is expected to be approachable and supportive while also being honest about expectations, gaps, and follow-through. This requires discretion, sound judgment, and the ability to give feedback without taking over the manager’s role.

The Lead also shares relevant observations and feedback with management, including recurring questions, learning needs, workflow barriers, service-quality concerns, and patterns affecting clients or teams. The Lead provides objective information and practical context; management remains responsible for supervisory and performance decisions.

Work may occur in CoHeWo offices, shelters, homes, clinics, community locations, partner sites, and outdoor settings, including areas where people experiencing homelessness live or receive services. The specific mix of settings depends on program and team needs.

A Day in the Life

You may begin your day by reviewing alerts and follow-up needs for clients on your assigned caseload. You might contact a client about a medical appointment, housing-related need, benefit, transportation barrier, or care-plan goal; coordinate with a health plan, provider, housing partner, or another member of the care team; and document the work in the required system.

Later, you may check in with a newly hired CHW, accompany them during a shadowing activity, review a service note for coaching, help CHWs from another department think through a complex client situation, respond to peer questions in a shared chat, or share an objective update with the Project Manager. You may also hold office hours for the Health and Homelessness Services team, provide coverage for an absent CHW, attend a partner meeting, or prepare a short learning activity for the team.

No two days will be exactly the same. The Lead must balance responsibility for their own clients with planned coaching, onboarding, documentation review, team coverage, and changing program needs. The Lead must also protect confidentiality and know when to coach, when to consult the manager, and when to involve another subject-matter expert.

What You’ll Do

As a Community Health Worker

Maintain an assigned caseload and serve as a consistent point of contact for clients, while coordinating with the broader team so support can continue when the Lead is unavailable.
Build trusted, respectful relationships with clients and engage them in identifying priorities, strengths, barriers, and next steps.
Complete required assessments and develop, update, and follow person-centered care plans, goals, or service plans in partnership with the client.
Coordinate integrated care and housing-related supports, including connections to medical care, behavioral health services, housing resources, benefits, transportation, food, employment, and other community services.
Initiate and follow up on referrals; communicate with health plans, providers, housing partners, community organizations, and other members of the client’s care team as authorized and appropriate.
Document contacts, assessments, plans, referrals, outcomes, and follow-up accurately and within required timelines using assigned systems and workflows.
Provide services in offices, homes, shelters, clinics, community locations, partner sites, and outdoor settings based on client, program, and team needs.

As a Lead: onboarding, shadowing, and skill development

Serve as a consistent mentor and resource for newly hired CHWs during their initial onboarding period.
Lead and participate in shadowing and reverse-shadowing activities that allow employees to observe, practice, receive feedback, and demonstrate readiness.
Model core CHW practices, including client engagement, assessments, goal setting, documentation, follow-up, professional boundaries, and use of required systems.
Provide one-on-one coaching, practical guidance, and timely feedback in coordination with the Project Manager.
Support targeted skill development identified by the manager while recognizing that formal performance management remains the manager’s responsibility.

As a Lead: quality and consistent practice

Review selected documentation or work products for coaching, peer-learning, and quality-improvement purposes.
Help CHWs understand program expectations and apply established workflows consistently.
Identify recurring questions, knowledge gaps, or process barriers and bring them to the Project Manager.
Support the development and updating of onboarding materials, training resources, practice tools, and standard workflows.
Participate in train-the-trainer opportunities and share learning with the team in a clear and practical way.

As a Lead: team coverage and problem-solving

Provide coverage during planned or unplanned absences and help address overflow or time-sensitive referrals when assigned.
Help colleagues think through complex client situations without taking sole ownership of another CHW’s responsibilities.
Communicate concerns involving client safety, service quality, boundaries, documentation, or role scope through the appropriate channels.

As a Lead: communication, training, and partnership

Provide regular, objective updates to the Project Manager about onboarding progress, demonstrated skills, learning needs, and barriers.
Develop and deliver trainings, practice activities, peer-learning discussions, and refreshers based on identified team and organizational needs.
Conduct scheduled office hours for the Health and Homelessness Services team to answer questions, support case consultation, and connect staff with the appropriate manager or subject-matter expert when needed.
Attend relevant health-plan, stakeholder, and community-partner meetings to stay informed and support alignment with program expectations.
Build respectful relationships with colleagues and partners and represent CoHeWo professionally.
Participate in supervision, Lead coordination, team meetings, training, and organizational learning activities.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role includes:

Clients on the Lead’s assigned caseload receive timely, person-centered support, coordinated services, accurate documentation, and consistent follow-through.
New CHWs understand expectations, receive meaningful practice, and know where to go for help.
Feedback is specific, respectful, timely, and focused on helping someone improve.
The Lead models the documentation, follow-through, boundaries, communication, and client-centered practice expected of the team.
Managers receive useful information without the Lead making supervisory or disciplinary decisions.
Training and coaching respond to actual patterns and learning needs rather than one isolated mistake.
Client services remain timely and consistent when coverage or overflow support is needed.
The Lead knows when to coach, when to consult, and when to escalate a concern.

What Can Be Challenging About This Work

The Lead is both a peer and a leadership resource. Coworkers may bring questions, frustrations, or mistakes to you, and you may need to offer honest feedback while preserving trust. At times, you may observe a concern that needs to be shared with the Project Manager even when the conversation feels uncomfortable.

The role also requires balancing responsibility for an assigned caseload with planned coaching and changing team needs. An onboarding activity may need to shift because one of your clients has an urgent need; a client follow-up may need to be coordinated around a shadowing activity, staff absence, or partner deadline. Supporting others does not remove the Lead’s accountability for timely follow-up, accurate documentation, continuity of care, appropriate boundaries, and required outcomes for their own clients.

The Lead is not expected to have every answer. Success requires recognizing the limits of your knowledge, avoiding unofficial policies or instructions, and involving the manager or appropriate subject-matter expert when guidance is needed.

How CoHeWo Supports You

CHW Leads are not expected to step into leadership without preparation. Support includes:

Clear expectations about the Lead’s authority, responsibilities, and relationship with the Project Manager.
Training and guidance on coaching, feedback, facilitation, documentation review, confidentiality, and professional boundaries.
Regular check-ins with the Project Manager to review priorities, onboarding progress, team needs, and difficult situations.
Access to program and subject-matter experts when questions exceed the Lead’s knowledge or role.
A generally smaller caseload than other CHWs in the same assignment to create time for defined Lead responsibilities.
Train-the-trainer and professional-development opportunities based on program and organizational needs.

Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Internal and external candidates will be considered for this vacancy. For the purposes of this vacancy, internal candidates are defined as staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded or ungraded contract, including Junior Professional Officers (JPOs), staff on Special Leave Without Pay (SLWOP), UN Volunteers with at least twelve (12) months of continuous service in IOM, and staff members on secondment/loan released by the Organization, unless otherwise specified in their contract. Staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded contract will not retain their contract type if appointed to an ungraded position.

Organizational Context and Scope

IOM operates Five Accommodation Centers for Unaccompanied Minors (Shelters) providing accommodation and access to services for Unaccompanied Migrant Children (UMC). Besides accommodation, the following services are provided to the beneficiaries: addressing basic needs, food, hygiene, legal counselling, and information about life opportunities in Greece, interpretation, psychosocial support, medical support, Greek learning programs, learning support, organization of intercultural activities, work and career guidance.

Responsibilities

Take the social history of the unaccompanied child.
Facilitate access to community services, social programs, and vocational education and training opportunities for minors, ensuring they benefit from available local and public resources.

Monitor the vaccination schedule of each minor.

In collaboration with the rest of the team, implement necessary actions for the achievement of the objectives of the Individual Action Plan in accordance with the best interests of the child.
In collaboration with the child's Guardian, conduct Best Interest Assessments (BIA) or prepare other similar reports and identify the needs and vulnerabilities of unaccompanied children.

Collect and monitor all the required beneficiaries’ documentation, on a monthly basis, for donor purposes.
Support the child in the Accommodation Center entry process, explain and discuss the rules of accommodation. Be their stable contact person and meet with the child at least once a week. Inform the child in advance of who will be responsible in case of each of your absences or leave.
Support the child in the smooth integration in activities inside or outside the Shelter.

About Community HealthWorks

Community HealthWorks (CoHeWo) advances health equity by helping individuals and families access the health coverage, care, and community services they need to thrive. We partner with health plans, health systems, government agencies, community-based organizations, and other service providers to remove barriers to care.

Community Health Workers are central to this work. They serve as trusted connectors who help people understand complex systems, identify their needs and goals, and take practical next steps toward greater health and stability.

Position Summary

The Community Health Worker, Pre-Release Care Manager (PCRM) works with people preparing to return to the community after incarceration. The CHW helps each person identify their health and social needs, understand available options, prepare for release, and connect with services that can support stability and continuity of care.

This role includes working inside Sacramento County correctional facilities and coordinating with clients, jail health staff, health plans, behavioral-health providers, housing and employment programs, justice partners, community organizations, and other CoHeWo teams.

The CHW helps develop and carry out individualized reentry care plans that reflect each client’s goals and priorities. Support may include healthcare, behavioral health, medications, medical equipment, housing, transportation, employment, health coverage, public benefits, and other community resources.

This is a non-clinical, non-supervisory role. While some assignments are supported through California’s CalAIM Justice-Involved initiative, CoHeWo’s reentry work may also include other programs, partnerships, and funding sources serving people preparing for or navigating a return to the community.

What This Work Looks Like

This role combines in-person work inside correctional facilities, client assessment and planning, documentation, communication across multiple systems, and coordination of services before and after release.

The CHW may meet with a client inside the Sacramento County Main Jail or Rio Cosumnes Correctional Center to understand their goals, health needs, living situation, benefits, employment interests, and anticipated needs after release. The CHW then works with the client and appropriate partners to develop practical next steps.

Release plans and circumstances may change quickly. A release date may move, a service may not be immediately available, or a client’s priorities may change. The work requires flexibility, accurate documentation, clear communication, professional boundaries, and the ability to coordinate with multiple partners without losing sight of the person at the center of the plan.

The CHW works as part of a team. Clients may work with one CHW over multiple interactions, but clear records and team communication allow another qualified team member to assist when needed.

A Day in the Life

You may begin your day by reviewing assigned client appointments, release information, follow-up tasks, and messages from CoHeWo colleagues or community partners. Before entering a correctional facility, you will follow all required check-in, identification, safety, and security procedures.

Inside the facility, you might meet with a client to discuss their health, medications, housing, employment, benefits, transportation, and personal goals for returning to the community. Together, you may identify priorities and document an individualized Reentry Care Plan.

Later, you may coordinate with jail health staff, a health plan, behavioral-health provider, housing program, pharmacy, probation or parole, or another community partner. You may initiate referrals, confirm appointment availability, help address missing information, or arrange a connection intended to take place after release.

You will also document services, client consent, referrals, coordination, and outstanding next steps in the required systems. No two days will look exactly the same, but preparation, accuracy, follow-through, and respect for both client autonomy and facility requirements are always part of the work.

What You’ll Do

Reentry planning and client support

Meet with clients preparing to return to the community and build respectful, person-centered relationships.
Listen to each client’s goals, priorities, strengths, concerns, and anticipated needs after release.
Complete required assessments and work with the client and appropriate partners to develop an individualized Reentry Care Plan.
Help clients understand available services, what can be arranged before release, and what steps may need to occur after release.
Update plans when release circumstances, client needs, or available resources change.
Support continued follow-through when a need cannot be addressed during one meeting or by one service provider.

Healthcare and community coordination

Initiate and coordinate referrals for medical, behavioral-health, pharmacy, durable medical equipment, and community-based services.
Help clients connect with housing, transportation, employment, health coverage, public benefits, and other social supports.
Coordinate with Sacramento County Adult Correctional Health, health plans, providers, justice partners, community-based organizations, and other CoHeWo teams.
Support timely connections to care and services following release.
Recognize when a need is outside the CHW’s role and involve an appropriate supervisor, clinical provider, subject-matter expert, or community partner.

Consent, confidentiality, and documentation

Explain and obtain required client consent for information sharing.
Protect client privacy and comply with HIPAA, confidentiality requirements, program standards, and organizational policies.
Maintain timely and accurate Reentry Care Plans, service notes, referrals, follow-up tasks, client consents, coordination records, and outcomes.
Use required CoHeWo, County, health-plan, and electronic health-record systems according to established workflows.
Document the client’s goals, assistance provided, outstanding items, and next steps so another team member can provide informed support when needed.

Facility safety and professional conduct

Follow all Sacramento Sheriff’s Office safety, custody, access, and security requirements while working inside correctional facilities.
Follow Sacramento County Adult Correctional Health policies, procedures, documentation standards, and electronic health-record workflows.
Maintain awareness of the correctional environment and follow staff instructions related to movement, access, prohibited items, emergencies, and client contact.
Maintain professional boundaries and communicate safety, security, confidentiality, or client-care concerns through the appropriate channels.
Participate in supervision, team meetings, training, consultation, and program data-quality activities.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role includes:

Helping clients understand and participate in their own reentry plans.
Developing plans that reflect the client’s goals while identifying practical next steps for health and stability.
Completing referrals and coordination early enough to support a safe transition when circumstances allow.
Providing accurate information and being clear about what CoHeWo can and cannot control.
Following through on commitments and communicating when release plans, services, or timelines change.
Creating clear records so clients can receive coordinated support without having to start over.
Working effectively with correctional, healthcare, community, and justice partners while keeping the client’s dignity and priorities at the center.
Following facility safety and security requirements consistently and knowing when to ask for guidance or escalate a concern.

What Can Be Challenging About This Work

People preparing to leave custody may be managing complex medical conditions, behavioral-health needs, substance use, housing instability, disrupted family relationships, employment barriers, or uncertainty about what will happen after release.

Release dates and circumstances may change with limited notice. Community services may have waitlists or eligibility requirements, and some resources may not be available when needed. A carefully developed plan may need to change quickly, and clients may make decisions that differ from what others recommend.

Working inside a correctional facility also requires strict adherence to security procedures. Entry may take time, access may be delayed or restricted, scheduled meetings may change, and employees must remain aware of their surroundings and follow facility instructions.

The work requires patience, adaptability, emotional steadiness, sound judgment, and professional boundaries. CHWs must remain helpful and respectful without taking sole responsibility for another system’s decision or a client’s outcome.

How CoHeWo Supports You

Employees are expected to ask questions and are not expected to navigate complex reentry situations alone. Support includes:

Structured onboarding, shadowing, and guided practice.
Required orientation and training for working inside correctional facilities.
Training on reentry planning, client navigation, confidentiality, consent, documentation, and required systems.
Regular supervision, consultation, and team-based problem-solving.
Access to colleagues with healthcare, behavioral-health, housing, benefits, and other subject-matter expertise.
Clear pathways for escalating clinical, safety, security, confidentiality, or coordination concerns.
Updated guidance when program, County, facility, health-plan, or community requirements change.

This remote role supports high-risk patients during the critical 30 days following hospital discharge.

You will provide short-term, telephonic, interdisciplinary care management focused on preventing avoidable readmissions.

The role combines clinical assessment, patient education, care coordination, and advocacy.

You will build individualized care plans that address medical, psychosocial, medication, and resource-related needs.

Working closely with nurses, physicians, social workers, primary care providers, and community resources, you will help patients navigate complex care journeys.

Connect patients with appropriate clinical services, community-based organizations, social support, durable medical equipment, and other resources.

Description

The Substance Use Disorder Professional/Case Manager (SUDP) will provide culturally relevant Substance Use Disorder (SUD) services to Tribal members and other clients. This position includes conducting assessments, creating treatment plans, offering counseling, and ensuring continuity of care through case management and follow-up.

Essential Duties

Provide substance use disorder services to Tribal members and other clients, including intakes, assessments, referrals, individual treatment plans, UAs, group and individual counselling and education and documentation of client care provided.
Serve as the lead with Tribal member requests for case management. Including but not limited to:
Requests for inpatient and/or referred care including emergency and/or crisis situations according to the policy and process in place to ensure the requests are processed quickly and the appropriate level of care is coordinated with external agencies and/or facilities.
Monitor care received from external agencies and/or facilities to ensure inpatient and/or residential care received is the appropriate level of care. If the Tribal member is returning to ambulatory care provided by Snoqualmie Behavioral Health Services (SBHS) or another agency, provide the client with transition planning.
Plan and implement follow-up or aftercare programs for Tribal members discharged from external agencies or facilities providing inpatient or residential care services, so continuity of care is in place.
Provide Tribal members with information about addiction issues and services/programs available, making appropriate referrals when necessary.
Attend relevant training sessions including evidence-based and promising practices for SUD and the provision of culturally relevant care to increase knowledge and skills.
Prepare for and participate in SBHS care management meetings and/or SBHS staff meetings that support Tribal member or client’s access to care and transition planning or support services.
Consistently document all care, education and case management provided in the electronic health record.
Update annual paperwork for clients receiving services.

Additional Duties

Attend clinical supervision meetings with SUDP’s and staff cases and/or conduct educational meetings including review of individual service plans, diagnosing and meeting medical necessity within client files; attend other meetings as designated by the clinical supervisor.
Maintain continuing education requirements per WAC 246-811 and develop a SUDP Enhancement Plan with the SUD Clinical Supervisor.
The Tribe values its commitment to community service and the well-being of its members. In recognition of this, each employee may be expected to perform duties from time to time which may not be related to their regular responsibilities.

To apply for this position:

About Community HealthWorks

Community HealthWorks (CoHeWo) advances health equity by helping individuals and families access the health coverage, care, housing support, and community services they need to thrive. We work at the intersection of healthcare and community support, partnering with managed care plans, health systems, community-based organizations, and government agencies to remove barriers to care.

Community Health Workers are central to this work. They serve as trusted connectors who help people understand complex systems, identify their own goals, and take practical next steps toward greater health and stability.

Position Summary

The Community Health Worker, CalAIM works primarily in the community with Medi-Cal members who may be experiencing homelessness, multiple chronic health conditions, behavioral health needs, substance use, or other barriers to care.

Through California’s CalAIM initiative, the CHW provides Enhanced Care Management, coordinated support for complex health and social needs, and Community Supports, including housing-focused services that help eligible members work toward stability. The CHW carries an active caseload and works closely with health plans, providers, housing and benefits systems, community partners, and other CoHeWo teams. This is a non-clinical, non-supervisory role.

What This Work Looks Like

This is a relationship-based, field-focused position. Approximately 60% of the work takes place in the community and 40% involves documentation, phone outreach, service coordination, team meetings, and follow-up. Work may occur in shelters, encampments, homes, clinics, hospitals, government offices, housing locations, and partner sites.

Plans may change during the day based on a member’s circumstances. The work requires flexibility, clear communication, sound judgment, and the ability to work independently while remaining connected and accountable to the team.

A Day in the Life

You may begin your day by reviewing your caseload, responding to messages, and coordinating with teammates or a health plan. You might then meet a member at a shelter, encampment, clinic, government office, or prospective housing location to complete an assessment, prepare for an appointment, replace an identification document, apply for benefits, or work through a setback in a care or housing plan.

Later, you may accompany a member to an important appointment, coordinate with a provider or partner, connect someone with an essential resource, and document the services provided. No two days will look exactly the same, but timely follow-through and accurate documentation are always part of the work.

What You’ll Do

Member engagement and direct support

Conduct in-person and telephone outreach to Medi-Cal members identified for Enhanced Care Management or Community Supports.
Build respectful, trusting relationships and help members identify their goals, understand their options, and take practical next steps.
Meet members in community settings and accompany them to medical, housing, benefits, and other important appointments when appropriate.
Connect members with essential resources such as food, clothing, water, shelter, transportation, and community-based services.
Provide support during urgent or emotionally difficult situations, follow organizational safety and escalation practices, and recognize the limits of CoHeWo’s non-emergency role.

Healthcare, Benefits, And Housing Coordination

Complete required health, housing, and social-needs assessments and develop service plans with members.
Help members obtain or maintain health coverage, establish primary care, follow up on healthcare needs, and communicate with health plans and providers.
Support housing navigation, including housing-readiness documents, referrals, applications, prospective housing opportunities, and move-in coordination.
Help members obtain identification, Social Security cards, income verification, and other documents needed to access services or housing.
Connect eligible members with behavioral health, substance-use, County Mental Health, System of Care, and other appropriate services.
Coordinate with CoHeWo teams and external partners to reduce gaps and duplication in services.

Documentation, communication, and teamwork

Maintain timely, complete, and accurate member records, service notes, assessments, activity logs, mileage logs, referrals, and required reports.
Use assigned electronic systems and standard office technology to track services, follow-up needs, and outcomes.
Protect member privacy and comply with HIPAA, confidentiality requirements, and organizational policies.
Participate in supervision, team meetings, case conferences, training, and community meetings.
Communicate changes, safety concerns, barriers, and situations requiring guidance to the appropriate supervisor or team member.

What Success Looks Like

Successful CHWs do not solve every problem for a member. They consistently help people understand their options, move toward self-identified goals, and remain connected to available support. Success in this role includes:

Building trust while respecting each member’s autonomy, privacy, and choices.
Following through on commitments and communicating when circumstances change.
Completing accurate documentation and required follow-up within established timelines.
Using sound judgment, professional boundaries, and organizational safety practices.
Working collaboratively and knowing when to ask for consultation or support.
Responding to setbacks with patience, curiosity, and a focus on practical next steps.

What Can Be Challenging About This Work

The people we serve may be navigating homelessness, serious health conditions, behavioral health needs, substance use, involvement with the justice system, or the effects of trauma. You may support someone through an urgent situation, witness difficult living conditions, experience setbacks after significant effort, or encounter circumstances that cannot be resolved immediately. Progress is rarely linear, and members may make choices that differ from what you would choose for them.

This work requires patience, emotional presence, adaptability, and professional boundaries. It also requires recognizing your own response to difficult circumstances, using supervision appropriately, and remaining effective without taking sole responsibility for another person’s outcome.

How CoHeWo Supports You

Employees are expected to ask for support and are not expected to navigate complex situations alone. Support for this role includes:

Structured onboarding, field shadowing, and reverse shadowing before independent work.
Regular supervision, case consultation, and team-based problem solving.
Training in core practices, professional boundaries, field safety, and required program systems.
Clear escalation pathways and guidance about the limits of the role.
Access to employee wellbeing and mental health resources available through CoHeWo’s benefits programs.

Requirements:

What We’re Looking For

Required

High school diploma or GED.
Ability to build respectful relationships with people from varied backgrounds and life circumstances.
Clear communication, organization, confidentiality, and consistent follow-through.
Comfort learning and using electronic documentation systems, email, and Microsoft Office tools.
Ability to work independently in community settings while remaining accountable and connected to a team.

Relevant Experience That May Help You Succeed

Relevant experience may come from paid work, volunteering, education, caregiving, community involvement, or lived experience that you choose to share. Applicants do not need to meet every preferred qualification to be considered. Helpful experience may include:

Community health, outreach, peer support, case management, health navigation, housing services, behavioral health, substance-use services, or work alongside people experiencing homelessness.
Knowledge of Medi-Cal, CalAIM, Sacramento’s housing and benefits systems, or local health and social-service resources.
Community Health Worker, peer-support, substance-use, behavioral-health, or health-coverage enrollment training or certification.
Postsecondary education in social work, behavioral health, public health, or a related field.

Requirements

Valid California Class C driver’s license, current auto insurance, reliable transportation, and ability to travel throughout Sacramento County and surrounding areas.
Completion of a criminal background check. Findings will be reviewed in relation to the position and in accordance with organizational policy and applicable law.
Compliance with health-screening, certification, safety, and partner-site requirements applicable to the assignment.
Maintenance of required training, certifications, and renewals associated with the role.

Work Environment & Schedule

This is a full-time, non-exempt position, typically Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required based on member or program needs. Work schedules are subject to change. Approved overtime will be compensated in accordance with applicable law and organizational policy.

Community-based work may involve variable weather, uneven terrain, noise, interruptions, animals, limited sanitation, or other environmental conditions. Employees are expected to assess conditions, follow field-safety practices, and consult a supervisor when circumstances exceed the role’s scope or can no longer be approached safely.

Physical & Emotional Demands

The employee must be able to frequently sit, stand, walk, speak, listen, use a computer, write, and operate standard office equipment. Fieldwork may include walking on uneven terrain. The employee may occasionally bend, stoop, kneel, reach, climb or balance, and lift or move approximately 10–15 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

The role includes regular interaction with people experiencing emotionally sensitive, urgent, or unpredictable circumstances. The employee must be able to communicate effectively, use sound judgment, maintain appropriate professional boundaries, follow safety and escalation procedures, and seek supervision or support when needed.

A resume describing your relevant experience and skills.
A brief cover letter explaining your interest in Community HealthWorks, what draws you to this position, and how your experience, skills, or perspective would help you contribute in the role.

We appreciate your interest in joining Community HealthWorks.

The Downtown Women’s Center (DWC) seeks full-time Case Manager - Housing with a proven history of high-quality intensive case management services provision, to provide culturally responsive services through the Housing Justice Program. The ideal candidate is focused on providing culturally responsive services to unhoused women, living on Skid Row, who have experienced long-term homelessness and have been historically underserved by traditional housing programs. This innovative program is dedicated to implementing the recommendations of the Ad-Hoc Committee on Black People Experiencing Homelessness and the Ad- Hoc Committee on Women Experiencing Homelessness and is designed to quickly and permanently house the most vulnerable women of Skid Row. The Specialist - Housing Justice is a collaboration between Downtown Women’s Center, the Mayor’s Office, City Council, and other homeless service sector partners. This role is responsible for providing intensive case management services, housing navigation, and conducting outreach to women in the Skid Row area. The Case Manager will be responsible for engaging women in services, building a caseload, establishing housing linkages and placement, and provide individualized case management using Housing First and Rapid Re-Housing Models. This position will report directly to the Housing Justice Program Supervisor.

Essential Functions

Provide culturally responsive field-based case management services to the most vulnerable women living in the Skid Row area to secure housing, including landlord engagement, identification of housing locations in the community, conducting biopsychosocial assessments, creating individual service plans, including goals to ensure housing stability, and ensuring women are linked to the appropriate services
Implement recommendations from the Ad-Hoc Committees on Black People Experiencing Homelessness, and Ad-Hoc Committee on Women Experiencing Homelessness, in providing services ranging from outreach, housing navigation, housing retention and connection with community resources
Collaborate with community service providers to identify appropriate clients through educational presentations and street outreach, as needed
Arrange transportation or provide transportation in personal vehicle, as needed, to ensure that clients are able to attend appointments
Research and provide necessary referrals for linkage with health care, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, food, employment, job training, public benefits and other services as indicated by treatment planning
Assist newly housed clients in familiarizing and connecting with community resources including but not limited to, local grocery stores, entertainment, transportation, health care and social supports and services

Work to effectively meet clients’ needs and resolve individual barriers through follow-up , advocacy and collaboration with DWC staff and other community service providers

Maintain accurate and timely records of activities, case management notes, and services provided to each participant

Description

FLSA Status:
Full-time, Non-Exempt

Compensation:
$28.00-$38.69 per hour
