Report to: Project Manager

To apply for this position:
Please submit a resume and cover letter. Your resume will not be considered if a cover letter is not included.

About Community HealthWorks

Community HealthWorks (CoHeWo) advances health equity by helping individuals and families access the health coverage, care, housing support, and community services they need to thrive. Community Health Workers are central to this work, serving as trusted connectors who help people understand complex systems and take practical next steps toward greater health and stability.

Position Summary

The Community Health Worker (CHW), Lead is an experienced CHW who continues to provide the full range of direct CHW services while also serving as a day-to-day practice resource for other CHWs. The Lead builds trusted relationships with clients, completes assessments, develops person-centered goals and service plans, coordinates care and housing-related supports, connects clients with resources, documents services, and follows through on identified needs.

In addition to maintaining an assigned caseload, the Lead supports onboarding, shadowing, coaching, consistent workflows, documentation quality, team coverage, and practical problem-solving. Because time is allocated to these Lead responsibilities, the Lead will generally carry a smaller caseload than other CHWs in the same assignment. Caseload size and complexity may vary based on client needs, staffing, program requirements, and team priorities.

This is a leadership role without formal supervisory authority. The Lead does not approve time off, issue corrective action, complete performance evaluations, or replace the Project Manager. Instead, the Lead observes work, models effective practice, offers clear and respectful feedback, identifies questions or learning needs, and communicates relevant themes to the manager.

This opportunity is currently assigned to CalAIM-funded services. CoHeWo uses a shared CHW Lead model across service areas, so assignments and specific responsibilities may evolve based on organizational, community, partnership, and funding needs. The common purpose is to provide person-centered CHW services while helping the team apply CoHeWo’s practices consistently.

What This Work Looks Like

This is a direct-service CHW position with additional Lead responsibilities. The Lead maintains relationships with assigned clients and is accountable for timely outreach, assessment, care planning, navigation, referrals, coordination, documentation, and follow-up. The current assignment includes integrated care and housing-related support for people who may have complex medical, behavioral health, housing, and social needs.

Alongside their own client work, a Lead may shadow a new employee, demonstrate how to complete an assessment or service note, coach someone through a difficult client interaction, review documentation for learning opportunities, provide team coverage, facilitate a short training, or participate in a partner meeting—all within the same week.

The Lead is expected to be approachable and supportive while also being honest about expectations, gaps, and follow-through. This requires discretion, sound judgment, and the ability to give feedback without taking over the manager’s role.

The Lead also shares relevant observations and feedback with management, including recurring questions, learning needs, workflow barriers, service-quality concerns, and patterns affecting clients or teams. The Lead provides objective information and practical context; management remains responsible for supervisory and performance decisions.

Work may occur in CoHeWo offices, shelters, homes, clinics, community locations, partner sites, and outdoor settings, including areas where people experiencing homelessness live or receive services. The specific mix of settings depends on program and team needs.

A Day in the Life

You may begin your day by reviewing alerts and follow-up needs for clients on your assigned caseload. You might contact a client about a medical appointment, housing-related need, benefit, transportation barrier, or care-plan goal; coordinate with a health plan, provider, housing partner, or another member of the care team; and document the work in the required system.

Later, you may check in with a newly hired CHW, accompany them during a shadowing activity, review a service note for coaching, help CHWs from another department think through a complex client situation, respond to peer questions in a shared chat, or share an objective update with the Project Manager. You may also hold office hours for the Health and Homelessness Services team, provide coverage for an absent CHW, attend a partner meeting, or prepare a short learning activity for the team.

No two days will be exactly the same. The Lead must balance responsibility for their own clients with planned coaching, onboarding, documentation review, team coverage, and changing program needs. The Lead must also protect confidentiality and know when to coach, when to consult the manager, and when to involve another subject-matter expert.

What You’ll Do

As a Community Health Worker

Maintain an assigned caseload and serve as a consistent point of contact for clients, while coordinating with the broader team so support can continue when the Lead is unavailable.
Build trusted, respectful relationships with clients and engage them in identifying priorities, strengths, barriers, and next steps.
Complete required assessments and develop, update, and follow person-centered care plans, goals, or service plans in partnership with the client.
Coordinate integrated care and housing-related supports, including connections to medical care, behavioral health services, housing resources, benefits, transportation, food, employment, and other community services.
Initiate and follow up on referrals; communicate with health plans, providers, housing partners, community organizations, and other members of the client’s care team as authorized and appropriate.
Document contacts, assessments, plans, referrals, outcomes, and follow-up accurately and within required timelines using assigned systems and workflows.
Provide services in offices, homes, shelters, clinics, community locations, partner sites, and outdoor settings based on client, program, and team needs.

As a Lead: onboarding, shadowing, and skill development

Serve as a consistent mentor and resource for newly hired CHWs during their initial onboarding period.
Lead and participate in shadowing and reverse-shadowing activities that allow employees to observe, practice, receive feedback, and demonstrate readiness.
Model core CHW practices, including client engagement, assessments, goal setting, documentation, follow-up, professional boundaries, and use of required systems.
Provide one-on-one coaching, practical guidance, and timely feedback in coordination with the Project Manager.
Support targeted skill development identified by the manager while recognizing that formal performance management remains the manager’s responsibility.

As a Lead: quality and consistent practice

Review selected documentation or work products for coaching, peer-learning, and quality-improvement purposes.
Help CHWs understand program expectations and apply established workflows consistently.
Identify recurring questions, knowledge gaps, or process barriers and bring them to the Project Manager.
Support the development and updating of onboarding materials, training resources, practice tools, and standard workflows.
Participate in train-the-trainer opportunities and share learning with the team in a clear and practical way.

As a Lead: team coverage and problem-solving

Provide coverage during planned or unplanned absences and help address overflow or time-sensitive referrals when assigned.
Help colleagues think through complex client situations without taking sole ownership of another CHW’s responsibilities.
Communicate concerns involving client safety, service quality, boundaries, documentation, or role scope through the appropriate channels.

As a Lead: communication, training, and partnership

Provide regular, objective updates to the Project Manager about onboarding progress, demonstrated skills, learning needs, and barriers.
Develop and deliver trainings, practice activities, peer-learning discussions, and refreshers based on identified team and organizational needs.
Conduct scheduled office hours for the Health and Homelessness Services team to answer questions, support case consultation, and connect staff with the appropriate manager or subject-matter expert when needed.
Attend relevant health-plan, stakeholder, and community-partner meetings to stay informed and support alignment with program expectations.
Build respectful relationships with colleagues and partners and represent CoHeWo professionally.
Participate in supervision, Lead coordination, team meetings, training, and organizational learning activities.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role includes:

Clients on the Lead’s assigned caseload receive timely, person-centered support, coordinated services, accurate documentation, and consistent follow-through.
New CHWs understand expectations, receive meaningful practice, and know where to go for help.
Feedback is specific, respectful, timely, and focused on helping someone improve.
The Lead models the documentation, follow-through, boundaries, communication, and client-centered practice expected of the team.
Managers receive useful information without the Lead making supervisory or disciplinary decisions.
Training and coaching respond to actual patterns and learning needs rather than one isolated mistake.
Client services remain timely and consistent when coverage or overflow support is needed.
The Lead knows when to coach, when to consult, and when to escalate a concern.

What Can Be Challenging About This Work

The Lead is both a peer and a leadership resource. Coworkers may bring questions, frustrations, or mistakes to you, and you may need to offer honest feedback while preserving trust. At times, you may observe a concern that needs to be shared with the Project Manager even when the conversation feels uncomfortable.

The role also requires balancing responsibility for an assigned caseload with planned coaching and changing team needs. An onboarding activity may need to shift because one of your clients has an urgent need; a client follow-up may need to be coordinated around a shadowing activity, staff absence, or partner deadline. Supporting others does not remove the Lead’s accountability for timely follow-up, accurate documentation, continuity of care, appropriate boundaries, and required outcomes for their own clients.

The Lead is not expected to have every answer. Success requires recognizing the limits of your knowledge, avoiding unofficial policies or instructions, and involving the manager or appropriate subject-matter expert when guidance is needed.

How CoHeWo Supports You

CHW Leads are not expected to step into leadership without preparation. Support includes:

Clear expectations about the Lead’s authority, responsibilities, and relationship with the Project Manager.
Training and guidance on coaching, feedback, facilitation, documentation review, confidentiality, and professional boundaries.
Regular check-ins with the Project Manager to review priorities, onboarding progress, team needs, and difficult situations.
Access to program and subject-matter experts when questions exceed the Lead’s knowledge or role.
A generally smaller caseload than other CHWs in the same assignment to create time for defined Lead responsibilities.
Train-the-trainer and professional-development opportunities based on program and organizational needs.

PATRAS"" with MIS Code 6016489 the Program "Greece Programme - Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund 2021-2027". Take the social history of the unaccompanied child.
Facilitate access to community services, social programs, and vocational education and training opportunities for minors, ensuring they benefit from available local and public resources.
Organize group and one-on-one sessions for the social support of the children, solving challenges that may arise during their accommodation, satisfying their requests or meeting their needs.

Support the continuous development of the abilities of each child, aiming at their gradual autonomy and the subsequent smooth transition to adulthood.
Complete and post on the website www.anynet.gr the Individual Family Rehabilitation Plan of the child.
Refer the beneficiaries to a primary or secondary medical care unit, if this is deemed necessary due to their state of health, as well as to a civil society organization or legal entity providing medical services.
Monitor the vaccination schedule of each minor.

About Community HealthWorks

Community HealthWorks (CoHeWo) advances health equity by helping individuals and families access the health coverage, care, and community services they need to thrive. We partner with health plans, health systems, government agencies, community-based organizations, and other service providers to remove barriers to care.

Community Health Workers are central to this work. They serve as trusted connectors who help people understand complex systems, identify their needs and goals, and take practical next steps toward greater health and stability.

Position Summary

The Community Health Worker, Pre-Release Care Manager (PCRM) works with people preparing to return to the community after incarceration. The CHW helps each person identify their health and social needs, understand available options, prepare for release, and connect with services that can support stability and continuity of care.

This role includes working inside Sacramento County correctional facilities and coordinating with clients, jail health staff, health plans, behavioral-health providers, housing and employment programs, justice partners, community organizations, and other CoHeWo teams.

The CHW helps develop and carry out individualized reentry care plans that reflect each client’s goals and priorities. Support may include healthcare, behavioral health, medications, medical equipment, housing, transportation, employment, health coverage, public benefits, and other community resources.

This is a non-clinical, non-supervisory role. While some assignments are supported through California’s CalAIM Justice-Involved initiative, CoHeWo’s reentry work may also include other programs, partnerships, and funding sources serving people preparing for or navigating a return to the community.

What This Work Looks Like

This role combines in-person work inside correctional facilities, client assessment and planning, documentation, communication across multiple systems, and coordination of services before and after release.

The CHW may meet with a client inside the Sacramento County Main Jail or Rio Cosumnes Correctional Center to understand their goals, health needs, living situation, benefits, employment interests, and anticipated needs after release. The CHW then works with the client and appropriate partners to develop practical next steps.

Release plans and circumstances may change quickly. A release date may move, a service may not be immediately available, or a client’s priorities may change. The work requires flexibility, accurate documentation, clear communication, professional boundaries, and the ability to coordinate with multiple partners without losing sight of the person at the center of the plan.

The CHW works as part of a team. Clients may work with one CHW over multiple interactions, but clear records and team communication allow another qualified team member to assist when needed.

A Day in the Life

You may begin your day by reviewing assigned client appointments, release information, follow-up tasks, and messages from CoHeWo colleagues or community partners. Before entering a correctional facility, you will follow all required check-in, identification, safety, and security procedures.

Inside the facility, you might meet with a client to discuss their health, medications, housing, employment, benefits, transportation, and personal goals for returning to the community. Together, you may identify priorities and document an individualized Reentry Care Plan.

Later, you may coordinate with jail health staff, a health plan, behavioral-health provider, housing program, pharmacy, probation or parole, or another community partner. You may initiate referrals, confirm appointment availability, help address missing information, or arrange a connection intended to take place after release.

You will also document services, client consent, referrals, coordination, and outstanding next steps in the required systems. No two days will look exactly the same, but preparation, accuracy, follow-through, and respect for both client autonomy and facility requirements are always part of the work.

What You’ll Do

Reentry planning and client support

Meet with clients preparing to return to the community and build respectful, person-centered relationships.
Listen to each client’s goals, priorities, strengths, concerns, and anticipated needs after release.
Complete required assessments and work with the client and appropriate partners to develop an individualized Reentry Care Plan.
Help clients understand available services, what can be arranged before release, and what steps may need to occur after release.
Update plans when release circumstances, client needs, or available resources change.
Support continued follow-through when a need cannot be addressed during one meeting or by one service provider.

Healthcare and community coordination

Initiate and coordinate referrals for medical, behavioral-health, pharmacy, durable medical equipment, and community-based services.
Help clients connect with housing, transportation, employment, health coverage, public benefits, and other social supports.
Coordinate with Sacramento County Adult Correctional Health, health plans, providers, justice partners, community-based organizations, and other CoHeWo teams.
Support timely connections to care and services following release.
Recognize when a need is outside the CHW’s role and involve an appropriate supervisor, clinical provider, subject-matter expert, or community partner.

Consent, confidentiality, and documentation

Explain and obtain required client consent for information sharing.
Protect client privacy and comply with HIPAA, confidentiality requirements, program standards, and organizational policies.
Maintain timely and accurate Reentry Care Plans, service notes, referrals, follow-up tasks, client consents, coordination records, and outcomes.
Use required CoHeWo, County, health-plan, and electronic health-record systems according to established workflows.
Document the client’s goals, assistance provided, outstanding items, and next steps so another team member can provide informed support when needed.

Facility safety and professional conduct

Follow all Sacramento Sheriff’s Office safety, custody, access, and security requirements while working inside correctional facilities.
Follow Sacramento County Adult Correctional Health policies, procedures, documentation standards, and electronic health-record workflows.
Maintain awareness of the correctional environment and follow staff instructions related to movement, access, prohibited items, emergencies, and client contact.
Maintain professional boundaries and communicate safety, security, confidentiality, or client-care concerns through the appropriate channels.
Participate in supervision, team meetings, training, consultation, and program data-quality activities.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role includes:

Helping clients understand and participate in their own reentry plans.
Developing plans that reflect the client’s goals while identifying practical next steps for health and stability.
Completing referrals and coordination early enough to support a safe transition when circumstances allow.
Providing accurate information and being clear about what CoHeWo can and cannot control.
Following through on commitments and communicating when release plans, services, or timelines change.
Creating clear records so clients can receive coordinated support without having to start over.
Working effectively with correctional, healthcare, community, and justice partners while keeping the client’s dignity and priorities at the center.
Following facility safety and security requirements consistently and knowing when to ask for guidance or escalate a concern.

What Can Be Challenging About This Work

People preparing to leave custody may be managing complex medical conditions, behavioral-health needs, substance use, housing instability, disrupted family relationships, employment barriers, or uncertainty about what will happen after release.

Release dates and circumstances may change with limited notice. Community services may have waitlists or eligibility requirements, and some resources may not be available when needed. A carefully developed plan may need to change quickly, and clients may make decisions that differ from what others recommend.

Working inside a correctional facility also requires strict adherence to security procedures. Entry may take time, access may be delayed or restricted, scheduled meetings may change, and employees must remain aware of their surroundings and follow facility instructions.

The work requires patience, adaptability, emotional steadiness, sound judgment, and professional boundaries. CHWs must remain helpful and respectful without taking sole responsibility for another system’s decision or a client’s outcome.

How CoHeWo Supports You

Employees are expected to ask questions and are not expected to navigate complex reentry situations alone. Support includes:

Structured onboarding, shadowing, and guided practice.
Required orientation and training for working inside correctional facilities.
Training on reentry planning, client navigation, confidentiality, consent, documentation, and required systems.
Regular supervision, consultation, and team-based problem-solving.
Access to colleagues with healthcare, behavioral-health, housing, benefits, and other subject-matter expertise.
Clear pathways for escalating clinical, safety, security, confidentiality, or coordination concerns.
Updated guidance when program, County, facility, health-plan, or community requirements change.

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

High school diploma or GED.
Ability to build respectful relationships with people from varied backgrounds and life circumstances, including people preparing to return to the community after incarceration.
Ability to listen, identify needs and goals, explain complex information clearly, and support practical next steps.
Clear communication, organization, confidentiality, attention to detail, and consistent follow-through.
Ability to work respectfully within both person-centered service practices and correctional-facility requirements.
Ability to coordinate with healthcare, government, justice, and community partners.
Comfort learning and using electronic documentation systems, email, Microsoft Office tools, and other assigned technology.
Ability to work independently while remaining accountable and connected to a team.
Ability and willingness to work regularly inside Sacramento County correctional facilities.

Relevant Experience That May Help You Succeed

Relevant experience may come from paid work, volunteering, education, caregiving, community involvement, or lived experience you choose to share. Applicants do not need to meet every preferred qualification to be considered.

new_jobs.title: Housing Case Manager
new_jobs.description:
The Housing Case Manager supports residents by developing Housing Service Plans and providing care coordination to ensure long-term housing stability. They also maintain a staff presence in buildings, intervene in crises, and collaborate with community providers to deliver trauma-informed support.

This is a unionized position represented by Local 8 of the Office and Professional Employees International Union (OPEIU). Starting wage is $36.10 an hour.

Job Summary

The Housing Case Manager (HCM) supports Plymouth residents by working as part of an onsite permanent supportive housing (PSH) team that is committed to supporting the well-being of residents and assists in maintaining high quality service delivery based on the values inherent in Plymouth’s mission, the principles of cultural proficiency, the tenets of harm reduction and trauma-informed care, and the ‘housing first’ philosophy. Specific tasks related to this position (but are not limited to) include support residents in their housing stability in identifying their housing stability barriers, partnering with residents to create Housing Service Plans, providing care coordination and supportive services to residents to meet their plan’s goals. This position also ensures there is a staff presence in buildings all while fostering a sense of community.

This position carries a designated caseload and is generally assigned to an individual Plymouth building but may be reassigned on a short- or long-term basis, based on business/service needs.

Work Schedule

This position may work up to a 40-hour work week (based on FTE), and at times requires working weekday evenings and one weekend day along with the willingness to work select holiday mornings.

Essential job functions: (Responsibilities, accountabilities, and competencies; may not include all duties of this job)

Supportive Services

In collaboration with each resident, develops and maintains a Housing Service Plan, which outlines goals that address transition needs and long-term housing stability needs of the resident in their new residence

Maintain extensive working knowledge of resources available to residents within Plymouth as well as public benefits and community organizations, ensuring that tenants access resources to the greatest extent possible.

Assists residents in scheduling appointments, arranging transportation, or transporting residents in Plymouth vehicle or rented vehicle to appointments; and accompany residents to appointments as appropriate

Advocate, consult and collaborate with community providers to ensure continuity of care.

Assists residents in moving into and/or out of their Plymouth housing as needed, following Plymouth policy and procedures.

Mediates conflict using de-escalation and other techniques.

Intervenes in crises, responds to emergencies, and initiates action as required, including contact with emergency response systems while focusing on the tenets of harm reduction and trauma-informed care.

Assists with resident complaints and concerns, escalating them to the Residential Services Manager (RSM) as needed.

Coordinate with the internal behavioral health team to support cohesive services to tenants.

Collaborative and Community Building

Attends and participates in scheduled supervision and team meetings to discuss resident issues and general program issues and goals.

Practices a cooperative work approach and promotes teamwork among co-workers and community partners; collaboration includes supporting community events and proactively aligning with building team on resident strategies

Collaborate with other Plymouth Housing Departments and/or participate in committees or workgroups as appropriate.

Provide backup to other Social Services staff in other buildings as needed, or backup front desk coverage on a regular or intermittent basis.

Provides a safe, sanitary environment in the buildings for tenants and staff.

Qualitative and Administrative

Work to the standard and requirements of the service program agreements, including program goals relating to residential stability; eviction prevention; enhanced income/skills and self-determination.

Maintains all database records and other required documentation in an accurate and timely manner including, by not limited to daily activities, progress notes, changes in resident status, etc. Follows strict confidentiality to protect resident’s private data.

Ensure significant events involving residents and building operations activities are recorded accurately in daily log and all necessary information during shift, reads log daily at start of shift; maintains and or assists with other program documentation as needed, .i.e., Incident Reports, and tenant satisfaction surveys

Records and maintains financial documentation as required for Plymouth credit card purchases on Resident behalf.

Follow program and agency policies and procedures. Provide input to program policies, procedures, and goals, as requested. Read materials as requested. .

Coordination with internal departments on activities, meetings and collecting resident information.

Essential job qualifications: (Any equivalent combination of knowledge, skills, abilities, education, and experience):

Education

BA/BS degree in a human service field. Advanced education can be substituted for experience and/or years of experience can be substituted for the required degree.

Experience

Minimum of two (2) years of experience working with homeless and low-income individuals, including persons living with mental and physical illnesses, chemical dependency/addictions, disabilities, HIV/AIDS.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Solid organizational and time management skills with ability to prioritize effectively and meet deadlines in a professional manner.
Self-motivated and ability to creatively problem solve.
Ability to develop and sustain successful relationships with tenants, community agencies and resources,
Empathic patience with individuals who are heavily impacted by addiction, mental health concerns, and trauma.
